title: Gideon and the Drop
premise: Dominic Fairweather, a fixer for the Meridian Office — an embassy that exists on no map — has spent two years unable to sleep since a botched extraction left his partner dead. When the office's off-book safe house appears on a real estate site with interior photos, Dominic realizes someone inside the network is selling them out, and the listing's timestamps encode coordinates for an attack staged to look like an infrastructure accident at a border checkpoint. Racing the shift change that will move security patterns and make the attack untraceable, Dominic teams with Lena Voss, the photographer whose innocuous listing broke the case open and who once loved him before duty came first. In the end Dominic exposes the mole at devastating personal cost, stops the attack minutes before the checkpoint shifts, and finally sleeps — choosing love over the office that consumed him.
about_author: Freya Eriksen is a former logistics analyst who spent a decade moving people and secrets across Nordic borders before turning to fiction. She writes from a farmhouse outside Bergen, where she claims the best plot twists arrive with the winter dark.

chapters.title: The House That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Insomnia-ridden, he runs a routine sweep of the office's digital footprint and finds Safe House Kestrel listed for sale — twelve interior photos, one showing a document box he personally burned. The beat is cold dread: invisibility was an illusion, and someone wanted him to see it.

chapters.title: Twelve Frames
chapters.summary: Lena Voss's POV. The architectural photographer who shot the listing insists she was hired anonymously through a broker and remembers a man watching her from a parked car. Reaching out to the only contact in the metadata — Dominic — she reopens a door both of them sealed years ago. The beat is wary reconnection laced with old grief.

chapters.title: Chain of Custody
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He traces the listing to a shell brokerage and finds the photo timestamps don't match the shoot date — they encode grid coordinates near the Halvard border checkpoint. His director orders him to stand down; the house is 'retired.' The beat is institutional betrayal: the office would rather bury him than investigate.

chapters.title: What the Night Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over one long sleepless night, Dominic and Lena reconstruct their shared past — the extraction that killed his partner Tomas, the choice Lena made to walk away rather than watch him disappear into the work. Memory becomes evidence: Tomas had flagged the same checkpoint weeks before he died. The beat is grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Decoding the timestamps fully, he learns the attack is scheduled for the exact window when the checkpoint's guard rotation changes — a gap engineered to look like human error, not sabotage. He goes off-grid to warn the checkpoint's commander, an old asset named Ilsa. The beat is the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Broker's Ledger
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Working the real estate trail alone, Lena identifies the broker as a cutout for someone inside the Meridian Office itself. She photographs the ledger connecting payments to Deputy Director Corven's private accounts — and realizes she's been followed since chapter two. The beat is terror transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: Kestrel Falling
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Lured back to the safe house under pretense of a debrief, Dominic walks into an ambush meant to close the loop. He escapes through the same rooms in the listing photos, using them like a map of his own betrayal, but Ilsa is killed covering his exit. The beat is survival at a price he can't stop counting.

chapters.title: Everything We Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Cornered in a freight yard, Dominic and Lena trade truths they've withheld: she kept copies of Tomas's final reports; he knew the office ordered the extraction compromised and said nothing. Love and accusation collide. They choose each other anyway, and plan to hit Corven where it hurts — the checkpoint itself. The beat is raw reconciliation.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, intercut with the attackers' approach. With forty minutes until the shift change, Dominic triggers the checkpoint's emergency protocol while Lena streams Corven's ledger to every intelligence service that will read it. The sabotage team is caught in the open; the attack collapses into a failed, very visible operation. The beat is breathless climax.

chapters.title: The Long Sleep
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, closing with Dominic's. Corven is arrested by the office's own auditors, desperate to contain the scandal; Dominic testifies, then resigns. Weeks later, in Lena's Bergen apartment, he sleeps through the night for the first time in two years — and wakes unafraid. The beat is quiet resolution: survival was never free, but it can finally be lived.
